audits.title: Evaluating the Quality of Medical Documentation at a University Teaching Hospital.
audits.standard: NHS Litigation Authority record keeping standards, CQC essential standards and Oxford University Hospitals documentation guidelines (VTE assessment within 6 hours, clear plan, postoperative instructions, senior present documented, contemporaneous entries)
audits.setting: University teaching hospital (inpatient notes; presented at the Nordic Orthopaedic Federation)

cycle1.result: VTE assessment within 6 hours 80% (available in 100%); plan and postoperative instructions 100%; contemporaneous entries 75%; consultant presence documented 80%

audits.intervention: Findings presented at the departmental audit meeting to raise awareness of contemporaneous documentation and recording the most senior person present

cycle2.result: Contemporaneous entries 89.11%; consultant presence documented 100%

audits.other_findings: Second cycle at 6 months: contemporaneous entries 80%, consultant presence 90%. Junior doctor presence was hard to establish and EPR timestamps make contemporaneous entry hard to judge.
audits.citation: Ridyard E, Street E. Evaluating the Quality of Medical Documentation at a University Teaching Hospital. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2015;4(1):u208052.w3253. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u208052.w3253. PMID: 26734328.

audits.title: 1310. Improving Infectious Disease Electronic Medical Records Documentation: A Quality Improvement Study in an Academic Teaching Hospital
audits.standard: Four-point note efficiency score; aim >50% improvement by May 2018
audits.setting: Infectious Disease Division, Tampa General Hospital, academic teaching hospital

cycle1.result: Mean note efficiency score 2.0 ± 0.84

audits.intervention: Needs assessment survey and education (cycle 1), then new standardised EMR note template with removal of auto-populated irrelevant information (cycle 2)

cycle2.result: Mean note efficiency score 3.6 ± 0.5

audits.other_findings: Cycle 1 score 2.8 ± 0.95 (n = 85); 95% template use; 42% improvement in ease of interpretation and 41% in adequate sign-out.
